news.title: Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense
paras: ICEYE, a satellite company, wants to buy Avio for more than two billion dollars. This would make Europe’s first fully integrated space company, meaning one firm built rockets and satellites together. Avio builds the Vega C rocket, which can carry small satellites up to three and a half tons into orbit. The Vega C has flown safely seven times in eight attempts since 2022. ICEYE also owns satellite machines that use radar to watch animals or weather worldwide. It sells this data to companies and governments, like Ukraine, that need information for safety. Europe wants its own space control so it does not rely on other countries.

Millions of pieces of space debris circle Earth at the moment, according to the European Space Agency (ESA). Even the smallest fragments are potentially dangerous, given how fast stuff travels in orbit.

Experts have proposed a range of measures to deal with this junk. The smallest bits, for example, may require big space nets, or lasering the stuff down to Earth. news.title: This Tiny, Unassuming Fungus Is a 'Dark Magic Mushroom'—the First Found to Contain Both Psychedelic Compounds
paras: Add as preferred source Galerina indica is smaller than a thumbnail. Kunik A little brown mushroom that grows in the swamps of Florida offers a lethal two-for-one deal: It can get you high and kill you.

The fungus Galerina indica , dubbed the “dark magic mushroom,” produces both the mind-altering chemicals psilocybin and psilocin, as well as deadly amatoxins, making it the first species of mushroom known to contain both types of compounds. The findings, published in the journal Current Biology on November 11, offer new understanding of the evolution and diversity of fungi.

sport.title: November 18, 1990: The day Monica Seles & Gabriela Sabatini played the first five-setter in women’s tennis in
paras: On this day in tennis history, Monica Seles and Gabriela Sabatini played out a monumental match. Look back on this historical moment in women’s tennis

On this day, November 18, 1990, Monica Seles defeated Gabriela Sabatini in the final of the Virginia Slims Championships (6-4, 5-7, 3-6, 6-4, 6-2) in a best-of-five sets final that went the distance. Seles’ triumph marked the first five-set match in women’s tennis since the 1901 US Nationals (the former name of the US Open ), when Elisabeth Moore had defeated Myrtle McAteer 6-4, 3-6, 7-5, 2-6, 6-2 in the final .
